messages:
sara_sales: Hey team — customer asked what exact artifacts we need to close the POC acceptance and get them over to legal for a pen-test signoff. also asked about staging IPs and whether dedicated pricing needs to be agreed before POC. short deadline: EOW.

mike_ps: Quick list that usually satisfies enterprise procurement: SOC 2 Type II summary (or attestation), ISO27001 cert if available, pen-test attestation/letter (signed by security/legal), network architecture diagram for UAT/staging, SSO integration docs (SAML metadata), list of staging IPs and firewall rules, data residency statement, and a short runbook for how we'll support the POC.

mike_ps: For pricing: we don't require a dedicated commit to run a POC, but if they want predictable latency we quote a reserved pool. ballpark: dedicated tier estimates depend on GPU class and throughput — i'll pull a tailored number once we know peak concurrency.

jordan_security: +1 on the artifact list. clarification on pen-test letter: we can provide a standard attestation template that says "penetration test completed within last 12 months with no critical findings" or a redacted summary report. prefer legal to sign delivery/attestation letters, but security can sign a technical attestation if customer insists.

jordan_security: We need to know whether customer accepts a redacted report vs full report in a secure dataroom. if they need full report, we'll require an NDA and limited access.

alex_sre: Staging IPs — for POC we typically provide ephemeral ranges and a short CIDR whitelist. we can open a 2-week window per test cycle. recommended pattern:
```
- UAT ingress: 54.32.10.0/28 (ephemeral)
- Control plane callbacks: 18.19.20.0/29
- Pre-signed uploads for artifacts + presigned URLs for test data
```
If they want static IPs for a longer window, that becomes an ops request and can affect pricing.

sara_sales: Helpful — can we convert this to a one-page acceptance checklist i can hand to the customer? they asked: "is network diag + SSO + pen-test letter enough to sign off?"

mike_ps: Short answer: usually yes, provided the pen-test attestation shows no critical/urgent findings and the SSO flow is functional in staging. here's a minimal acceptance checklist you can give them:
- SOC 2 Type II attestation OR signed summary of controls
- Penetration test attestation (template attached) OR redacted summary report in dataroom
- Network architecture diagram covering UAT/staging and any on-prem connectors
- SSO/SAML test user that successfully logs into the app in staging
- KMS/crypto separation statement if they require key custody guarantees
- Confirmation of staging IP whitelist or VPN details
- Agreed POC support hours and escalation contact

mike_ps: Note on pen-test language: we require an attestation that there are no outstanding critical vulnerabilities and a remediation timeline for any high findings. if the customer needs our internal vendor/scan provider info we can provide an attestation rather than raw scan artifacts.

jordan_security: I'll attach the standard pen-test attestation template in a follow-up message and can redline if their legal asks for tweaks. also: which internal person will sign? security prefers to sign technical attestation; legal should sign contractual addenda.

sara_sales: i'll ask the customer for their CISO + legal contact. they said their security manager ("Aisha Khan, CISO") can sign, but legal prefers to sign too. will confirm today. thanks all :thumbsup:

alex_sre: if they opt for static IP ranges for a month during POC, ops needs ~3 business days lead time. ping me if they want that and i'll open a ticket.

sara_sales: perfect — i'll send the checklist + ask about redacted vs full report and get back. tagging you all if they push on a full report or dedicated pricing.

mike_ps: sounds good. happy to jump on a quick call with the customer to walk the checklist.

jordan_security: prepared to review/redline the attestation once you have the customer's legal contact.

sara_sales: thanks!
